sentences.text: Revenue rose from $65.1 billion in FY2017 [F1] to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F10], a 3.3% CAGR [F201].
Operating income compounded faster at 4.1% [F202], while net income managed only 0.5% [F203] and diluted EPS 1.9% [F205].
Operating margin fell to 8.1% [F23] in FY2019 after an $8.35 billion non-cash Shave Care impairment [X112], which the filing ties to currency devaluations and slowing grooming categories [P62].
Margin rebounded 14.0pp to 22.1% in FY2020 [D160][F24] as operating income rose 186.2% [D148], with the prior-year charge lapping [P71].
Non-US geography added 3.1pp of the 3.3% FY2026 growth [D511][D457], and makes up 52.0% of revenue [D509].
Beauty grew 7.1% [D602], adding 1.3pp [D603], the largest segment contribution; US sales grew only 0.2% [D535].
Sales growth of 3.3% [D457] reflects favorable foreign exchange and pricing, with unit volume unchanged [P26].
Operating income fell 3.4% [D458] on 3.3% revenue growth [D457], an incremental margin of -25.6% [D481].
Diluted EPS grew 1.7% [D461] against net income growth of 0.5% [D459], with a 1.3% lower share count helping [D476].
Operating margin of 22.7% [F30] is above the 22.1% window median [D648] but below the 24.3% high [D647].
Cost of revenue took 1.0pp [D483] and SG&A 0.6pp [D485] off operating margin.
Operating margin fell 1.6pp [D470] mainly because gross margin dropped on product mix and commodity costs [P9] and marketing spending rose [P25].
Net margin of 18.4% [F50] is 4.3pp below operating margin [F30].
The effective tax rate of 20.8% [D443] rose on lower share-based compensation benefits and unfavorable geographic mix [P23].
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion [F80] was 1.22x net income [D444], but free cash flow was only 0.94x [D445].
Free cash flow of 0.94x net income [D445] sits below the 1.02x window median [D660].
Operating cash flow grew 9.8% [D462] on a near-neutral working capital effect, as inventory absorbed cash for safety stock [P3].
Capex reached 5.1% of revenue [D440] and 1.40x D&A [D446], with a $4.62 billion investing outflow [F110].
Net debt was $24.2 billion [D450], or 27.8% of revenue [D451], ranking at the 33rd percentile among six staples peers [D676].
Net cash rose $730 million [D399][D450], from -$24.9 billion [D399] to -$24.2 billion [D450], as cash rose 4.0% [D466] and total debt fell 1.0% [D478].
Buybacks and dividends totalled $15.3 billion [D452], 100.7% of free cash flow [D453], up from 86.6% in FY2024 [D350].
Payouts above free cash flow leave little room for further deleveraging unless cash conversion recovers, with long-term debt down 8.6% [D468].
Payouts exceeded free cash flow in nine of ten years [D350][D402][D453], a medium-severity, persistent flag; the filing gives no reason for the payout level.
Operating income fell 3.4% [D458], the largest drop outside FY2019 [D97], which the filing blames on lower gross margin and higher marketing spending [P25].
Days inventory rose from 52 [D21] to 69 [D455], and inventory grew 8.2% [D480] against revenue growth of 3.3% [D457].
The current ratio of 0.68x [F180] is below 1.0x, but it has stayed between 0.63x [D661] and 0.88x [D662] across the window, so it is structural rather than new.
Operating margin staying at or above the 22.1% window median [D648] in the FY2027 10-K would confirm the recovery; a fall below it would reverse it.
Buybacks and dividends falling back toward the FY2024 level of 86.6% of free cash flow [D350] would confirm slowing payouts; a figure above the latest 100.7% [D453] keeps the gap open.
Free cash flow returning to the 1.02x window median of net income [D660] while days inventory fall back from 69 [D455] would confirm conversion recovery.
